name: MonarchSavedViews
title: SavedViews
wrapsNative: MonarchButton (androidx.compose.material3.Button) with androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuItem and RadioButton; androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog with MonarchTextField for naming and confirming
summary: A menu button that switches between named views of a list (filters, sort and columns), with an Edited marker and actions to save, save as new, discard, rename, set the default and delete.
whenToUse: Above a list, table or board where people save combinations of filters, sort and columns under a name and come back to them.
whenNotToUse: For a fixed set of tabs use a Material 3 TabRow. For a single sort or filter choice use a menu button (DropdownMenu) or MonarchRolePicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchSavedViews(views: List<MonarchSavedView>, selectedId: String?, onSelect: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, modified: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, maxNameLength: Int = 80, trailingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchSavedViewsLabels = MonarchSavedViewsLabels(), onSaveNew: (suspend (String) -> Unit)? = null, onSaveChanges: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, onDiscardChanges: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRename: (suspend (String, String) -> Unit)? = null, onDelete: (suspend (String) -> Unit)? = null, onSetDefault: ((String) -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchSavedView(id: String, name: String, count: Int? = null, shared: Boolean = false, default: Boolean = false, readOnly: Boolean = false, group: String? = null)

class MonarchSavedViewsLabels(view, noView, modified, shared, defaultView, views, saveChanges: ((String) -> String)?, saveAsNew, discardChanges, rename, setDefault, delete, saveTitle, renameTitle, name, save, cancel, nameRequired, nameTaken, saveFailed, deleteTitle: ((String) -> String)?, deleteMessage, deleteConfirm, deleteFailed), every parameter optional and String? unless noted

options.name: views
options.description: The views in menu order, each with an id, a name and optionally a count, shared, default, readOnly and a group.

options.name: selectedId
options.description: The id of the selected view, or null for none (the button then reads "All items").

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the id of the chosen view; apply its filters, sort and columns.

options.name: size
options.description: The size of the menu button. The web's xs is Sm; the touch target is 48dp at every size.

options.name: modified
options.description: The list differs from the selected view: shows an Edited badge and offers to save or discard.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the menu can be opened.

options.name: maxNameLength
options.description: The longest name the naming field accepts; longer input is cut while typing.

options.name: trailingIcon
options.description: A decorative icon at the end of the button, such as a down chevron. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the button, the menu items, the dialog titles, the validation and failure messages and the delete confirmation.

options.name: onSaveNew
options.description: Stores the current state under the trimmed name and selects it. Offers "Save as new view…". The dialog stays open until it returns.

options.name: onSaveChanges
options.description: Saves the current state into the view with the id. Offered when modified and the view is not read-only.

options.name: onDiscardChanges
options.description: Reapplies the selected view. Offered when modified.

options.name: onRename
options.description: Renames the view with the id to the trimmed name. Offered for a selected view that is not read-only.

options.name: onDelete
options.description: Deletes the view with the id after the person confirms. Offered for a selected view that is not read-only.

options.name: onSetDefault
options.description: Makes the view with the id open by default. Offered for a selected view that is not already the default.

states.name: selected
states.description: The button shows the view's name and count; in the menu the view's radio button is selected.

states.name: edited
states.description: A warning badge reading "Edited" after the name, and Save changes and Discard changes in the menu.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Save changes, Rename and Delete are not offered.

states.name: naming
states.description: A dialog with a Name field; Save shows "Enter a name." or "A view with this name already exists." under the field, and a busy spinner while the callback runs.

states.name: deleting
states.description: A dialog titled "Delete “Open deals”?" with a danger Delete view button and Cancel.

states.name: failed
states.description: A thrown error keeps the dialog open with "The view could not be saved. Try again." or "The view could not be deleted. Try again."

states.name: disabled
states.description: The button takes its disabled colors and the menu does not open.

appearance: The button is a secondary MonarchButton; the count is in the muted text color and Edited is a warning badge. The menu and dialogs take the theme's raised surface; Delete view is in the strong danger color and its confirm button is the danger variant. High contrast themes use their stronger roles.
platformNotes: The web keeps its dialogs open while a returned promise is pending; on Android onSaveNew, onRename and onDelete suspend, so the dialog stays open with a busy button and shows a failure when they throw, as on the web (iOS uses system alerts and synchronous callbacks instead). onSaveChanges, onDiscardChanges and onSetDefault are menu actions that return at once; the app reports their failures. The web's visually hidden "View:" prefix is the button's content description "View". The web's star for the default view is the words "Default view", because Monarch bundles no icons. The web's uncontrolled defaultValue is not offered: state is hoisted. A delete failure has its own message here; the web reuses the save failure. iOS builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The menu button is named "View"; its state description is the selected view's name followed by "Edited" when modified.
Edited is a word in a badge, not only a color.
In the menu each view has the selected state and a radio button; its count, Shared and Default view are read as its second line.
Group headings in the menu have heading semantics.
The naming and delete steps are dialogs with a Cancel button; the back gesture cancels them unless a save is running.
The button has a touch target of at least 48 by 48dp and its text scales with the font size setting.
edgeCases: Only actions with a callback are offered; with no callbacks the menu only switches views.
Names are trimmed before they are passed to onSaveNew and onRename, and cut to maxNameLength while typing.
Renaming a view to its own name in another case is allowed.
Choosing the selected view again only closes the menu.
A long view name stays on one line in the button and ends with an ellipsis; the full name is in the menu and in what TalkBack reads.

examples.title: Views with filters, save and discard
examples.webExample: Views with filters, save and discard
examples.template:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3)) {
    MonarchSavedViews(
        views = views,
        selectedId = selected,
        onSelect = { selected = it },
        size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm,
        modified = {{modified}},
        onSaveNew = { _ -> },
        onSaveChanges = {},
        onDiscardChanges = {},
        onRename = { _, _ -> },
        onDelete = { _ -> },
        onSetDefault = {},
    )
    MonarchChip(text = "{{chip.name|raw}}: {{chip.value|raw}}", onRemove = {}, size = MonarchTagSize.Sm)
}
examples.setupTemplate:
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>({{selected}}) }
val views = listOf(
    MonarchSavedView({{views.0.id}}, {{views.0.name}}, count = {{views.0.count}}, readOnly = {{views.0.readOnly}}, group = {{views.0.group}}),
    MonarchSavedView({{views.1.id}}, {{views.1.name}}, count = {{views.1.count}}, readOnly = {{views.1.readOnly}}, group = {{views.1.group}}),
    MonarchSavedView({{views.2.id}}, {{views.2.name}}, count = {{views.2.count}}, default = {{views.2.isDefault}}, group = {{views.2.group}}),
    MonarchSavedView({{views.3.id}}, {{views.3.name}}, count = {{views.3.count}}, shared = {{views.3.shared}}, group = {{views.3.group}}),
)
examples.setup:
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>("mine") }
val views = listOf(
    MonarchSavedView("all", "All tickets", count = 64, readOnly = true, group = "Built-in"),
    MonarchSavedView("open", "Open", count = 18, readOnly = true, group = "Built-in"),
    MonarchSavedView("mine", "My open tickets", count = 7, default = true, group = "My views"),
    MonarchSavedView("team", "Team backlog", count = 23, shared = true, group = "My views"),
)
examples.code:
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3)) {

        views = views,
        selectedId = selected,
        onSelect = { selected = it },
        size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm,

        onSaveNew = { _ -> },

        onDiscardChanges = {},
        onRename = { _, _ -> },
        onDelete = { _ -> },

    )
    MonarchChip(text = "Status: Open", onRemove = {}, size = MonarchTagSize.Sm)

examples.title: Switching only
examples.code:
MonarchSavedViews(
    views = listOf(MonarchSavedView("mine", "Assigned to me"), MonarchSavedView("team", "My team")),
    selectedId = selected,
    onSelect = { selected = it },
    size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm,
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web names this control with one sentence ("View: My open tickets"). On Android TalkBack gets the control name and its current value as the control's name and state description ("View", "My open tickets"), which it speaks as one phrase and announces again when the value changes; the same words are visible in the control.
parityExceptions.convention: a control has a name and a state, not a joined sentence (Android accessibility: contentDescription + stateDescription)
